newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait halves projected 1995/96 deficit - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait halves projected 1995/96 deficit - newspaper.

text.p: Kuwait slashed a projected 1.32 billion dinar deficit for the fiscal year 1995/6 ending on June 30 to about 600 million dinars ($2.0 billion), a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
"Our economy has recovered, and the deficit fell to (about) 600 million dinars in 1995/96," al-Qabas newspaper said in a report based on remarks by Finance Minister Nasser Abdulla al-Rodhan.

Kuwait has said it plans to balance the budget by 2000 after suffering huge losses during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis. The tiny, oil-rich state incurred hefty costs during the 1991 Gulf War which ended its seven-month occupation by Iraq.
The paper, which did not have direct quotes from Rodhan, said the deficit cut resulted from a decline in state spending and increased revenue.
The finance minister had earlier said that higher than expected oil prices and lower state spending were expected to lead to a sharp drop in the state budget gap.
The government had projected spending of 4.23 billion dinars and revenues of 2.91 billion dinars in 1995/96. It adopted a conservative estimate of $13 a barrel of oil, Kuwait's main revenue earner.
Parliament earlier this month passed a 4.2 billion dinar budget for fiscal 1996/97 with a forecast net deficit of 1.2 billion dinars. ($1 = 0.299 dinar)
